rounds.text: Quest Capital Markets Ltd is profoundly under-appreciated, trading at a deeply discounted price-to-book ratio of 0.26x against a massive underlying book value of ₹ 1,051 per share, with the market capitalization resting at just ₹ 270 Cr [E2, E3]. This severe mispricing is further highlighted by a cheap P/E ratio of 10.43x that sits at roughly half of the sector benchmark of 20.21x, alongside a price-to-book of 0.35x that compares favorably to its sector benchmark of 1.35x [E6, E7]. Crucially, this discount does not stem from inferior operational efficiency, as the company generates a Return on Assets of 3.31%, nearly double the sector benchmark of 1.77% [E8]. Conceded: the company has delivered a poor compounded sales growth of -7% over the past five years and a recent year-over-year sales decline of 96% [E15, E68].

Conceded: the company trades at a P/B ratio of 0.26x to 0.35x and a P/E of 10.43x to 11.5x, which superficially looks cheap compared to sector benchmarks of 1.35x and 20.21x [E1, E2, E6, E7]. However, this deep discount is fully justified by severe top-line decay, evidenced by a compounded sales growth of -7% over the past five years and -1% over the past three years [E15, E16]. Furthermore, the company suffers from a catastrophic recent drop in demand, registering a year-over-year sales collapse of 96% [E68]. While the bull points to a 3.31% ROA and recent TTM sales growth [E8, E17], these short-term metrics mask a broader trend of decelerating earnings growth and a multi-year stagnation pattern [E15, E16, E69]. The market capitalization of ₹ 270 Cr against a seemingly massive book value is therefore a permanent value trap rather than a margin of safety, given that the underlying business is shrinking instead of compounding [E2, E3, E15, E68].
